speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your skin condition, have you noticed any new lesions, and if so, how long have they been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The history of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penis in a 62-year-old male smoker, particularly with a lesion on the finger (chronic skin irritation), is highly suspicious for malignancy. Previous failed treatments for syphilis and eczema suggest this is not an infectious or simple inflammatory process. Given the location and chronicity, we must prioritize ruling out invasive cancer.

REQUEST TEST: Penile Biopsy, Finger Biopsy.
REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of penile and digital lesions.
